title: Climb anyway (Leviticus Rabbah 29:2)
hook: Jacob sees the nations' angels climb and fall, and fears to climb
tomorrow: why would God speak from a scraggly thorn bush?

segments.voice: Yesterday: the stones became one, and Jacob slept on peace. Now he dreams, and the dream has a ladder in it.

Watching other people fall teaches its own lesson. A friend's big plan folds. A cousin's move across the country goes bad. You start to think: why try? Jacob, asleep on that stone, dreams of "a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven; and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it." Leviticus Rabbah says he watched who climbed, and who came down.
screen: `WATCHING OTHERS FALL.` → `A LADDER TO HEAVEN.` → `WHO CLIMBS? WHO COMES DOWN?`

segments.voice: In this midrash, the angels are the guardian princes of great empires. One climbs a long way, and comes down. Another climbs, and comes down. Another, and another. Then the Holy One says to Jacob: you, climb. And Jacob is afraid. Will I come down like them? The midrash lets two voices speak. Jacob's first. I've just watched every climber fall. Caution isn't cowardice; it's evidence. Who climbs a ladder that throws everyone off? His case is honest about what he saw. Then God's. You aren't them. Rabbi Meir says it with a sting: had you believed and climbed, you would never have come down. Fear kept the ladder empty. And the midrash doesn't leave Jacob there. He asks: then will my children be stuck down here forever? God answers with words from Jeremiah: fear not, Jacob My servant. Both voices are inside the text. The careful one, who learns from falls. The daring one, who says your path isn't theirs. The midrash gives God the last word, and the last word is gentle. No scolding. Fear not.
screen: `EMPIRES CLIMB, AND FALL.` · `JACOB: WHY CLIMB AT ALL?` · `GOD: YOU ARE NOT THEM.` · `FEAR NOT, JACOB.` · then, large: `CLIMB ANYWAY.`

segments.voice: Stand, if you can, feet together. Slowly rise onto your toes, the smallest climb there is, hold it while it's steady, then come down gently and rise again. Each time you rise, name one step you've been afraid to take. If standing doesn't work for you, lift your chin and shoulders instead.
Climb anyway: God's word to Jacob in Leviticus Rabbah, after he watched others fall. The text answers fear with fear not.
For the road: climb anyway, since other people's falls aren't your ladder. Day fifteen seventy-eight.

notes: Leviticus Rabbah 29:2 paraphrased. The midrash names the empires (Babylon, Media, Greece, Edom) and gives numbers of rungs; both left out under the claims rule. Confirm that 'Rabbi Meir' is the right attribution for 'had you believed and climbed' (cited via Rabbi Berechiah and Rabbi Helbo in some editions).
Debate shape: Jacob's caution and God's 'climb' each given a best case; the midrash's own ending (Jeremiah 30:10) is gentle. The exile theme is kept light.
